newsitem.title: INDIA: India's finance minister strong for economy reform.
newsitem.headline: India's finance minister strong for economy reform.

text.p: Palaniappan Chidambaram, who returned as India's Finance Minister on Thursday, is dedicated to opening up the huge country's economy and has won praise for breathing new life into a flagging reform programme.

The 51-year-old Harvard-educated Chidambaram joined Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 11-day-old centre-left government after being finance minister in the administration of Gujral's predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda.
A lawyer by profession, Chidambaram will put his free-trade stamp on the new coalition government, which is backed among others by communists.
The full measure of his commitment to a more open economy and his political acumen was apparent when he presented the government's budget on February 28.
The budget for 1997/98 (April-March) cut personal tax rates, lowered corporate taxes and slashed import duties.

Twice commerce minister under former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao who ruled from 1991 until last May, Chidambaram joined hands with the then finance minister Manmohan Singh to propel reforms forward.
The goverment introduced reforms in 1991 which swept away a battery of restrictions on trade and business in India's decades-old protected economy.
Chidambaram reluctantly resigned in 1992 after admitting his wife had unwittingly invested family funds in a company under investigation in India's biggest financial scandal.

The suave, bespectacled Chidambaram came back in 1995 and resigned again in April 1996 after his Congress party, then headed by Rao, forged a controversial regional electoral alliance in his southern state of Tamil Nadu.
A defiant Chidambaram helped to float a rival regional party, the Tamil Maanila Congress, and won a seat in parliament in the general election held in stages in April and May 1996.
His party allied with United Front, a coalition of regional, left and centrist parties which formed a minority government with the support of Congress after inconclusive polls.
Gujral's predecessor H.D. Deve Gowda inducted Chidambaram as a finance minister.
Deve Gowda's government lost a confidence vote in parliament in April after Congress party withdrew support. The United Front replaced Deve Gowda with Gujral.
Chidambaram's party stayed out of the government after its leader was bypassed in the leadership race, but reversed its stand, paving way for Chidambaram to join Gujral's cabinet.
Chidambaram, who sports neatly oiled hair and a crisp, starched white wraparound cloth "dhoti", is a quick-witted -- and often harsh -- advocate of economic liberalisation.
He first joined the government in 1985 as a junior minister in the commerce ministry, later moving to the personnel ministry and the home (interior) ministry under then prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.
When Rao reinstated him in a February 1995 cabinet reshuffle, Chidambaram unleashed a new series of trade reform policies.
Born into a wealthy family of textile barons on September 16, 1945, Chidambaram is married to Nalini, a lawyer. They have one son.
